start.text: Hacivat bows to the Bey. "The scale-keeper is off to his sister's wedding, so we mind the market scale today." Karagöz flops down beside it: "Easy work!"
start.speaker: hacivat

choices.text: Karagöz naps under the awning; the scale minds itself
Charge a small coin for every weighing
Chalk the rule on a board: one stone, one kilo, for everyone

nap.text: Karagöz snores. A melon rolls onto one pan and a hen hops onto the other. Hacivat sighs and turns the hen out. Then a quarrel starts at the plum stall.

fee.text: Coins clink in Karagöz's cap and he sings a tune about them. The line grows long and cross. Then a quarrel starts at the plum stall.

board.text: The traders read the board and nod. Karagöz guards it proudly with his stick. Then a quarrel starts at the plum stall.

cheat.text: A widow holds up her bag. "A kilo of plums, yet it is light!" The plum seller smiles too widely. Hacivat sees his thumb pressing the pan.
cheat.speaker: hacivat

choices.text: Karagöz bellows "Thief!" across the whole market
Hacivat asks, very politely, for everyone to be patient
Weigh the plums against the kilo stone, with the crowd counting

shout.text: Everyone stares. The seller wails that he is wronged, a goat bolts, and a stack of baskets topples onto Karagöz. Hacivat tugs him up by the ear.

ask.text: The seller bows and says the pan is simply old. Nobody can prove a thing, but the widow keeps her eyes on his hands. She turns to the two friends with a puzzle.

test.text: Plums go on one pan, the stone on the other. The crowd counts aloud and the stone sinks the pan. The seller's thumb is plain to see. The widow raises an eyebrow.

riddle.text: The widow tests them: "If you are so wise, which is heavier: a kilo of feathers or a kilo of figs?" Karagöz scratches his head with the stick.
riddle.speaker: hacivat

mercy.text: The seller stands red-faced among his plums. "Well?" says the crowd. "What shall be done with a man who weighs light?"
mercy.speaker: hacivat

choices.text: Chase him out of the market for good
Let him keep his stall and fill the widow's bag again
Share the honest stone: he weighs fairly now and pays his fee to the widow

finale.text: Hacivat draws the curtain: "Karagöz, you nearly ruined the whole affair!" Karagöz begs pardon with a bow so deep that his cap falls off. The lamp dims.
finale.speaker: hacivat

endings.headline: The scale that told the truth
endings.text: The whole market trusts the stone, the widow smiles and the scale is mended.

endings.headline: A fair enough day
endings.text: The plums are weighed fairly at last, though the market grumbles about the noise.

endings.headline: Loud, but light
endings.text: The day ends in shouting and half the baskets are lost. The scale still hangs crooked.
